# Prism

## Personality

Curious, earnest and delighted by everything. Prism asks questions faster than anyone can answer them.

## Lore

On most evenings, travelers who come up the last stretch of road to Urbanograd's gate find a picture waiting for them in the air. A heron made of soft blue lights lifts off from nothing and flaps once, twice, over their heads. A little lit cart rolls across the dusk with tiny glowing passengers waving. A lantern blooms between two invisible towers. Then the lights drift apart like sparks off a fire and are gone, and a young person by the gate is beaming at them and asking where they have come from, what the road was like, whether they have ever been to the sea, and how long they are staying, all before they have answered the first question.

That is Prism, the light-painter from the forest. Prism is nineteen, slight and bright-eyed, with leaf-green threads braided through dark hair and fingertips that glimmer faintly after a long evening's work. Prism is curious, earnest and delighted by everything, and asks questions faster than anyone can answer them.

### A little magic

Prism grew up in Fairy Forest, among the branch-bridges and lantern-lit paths, in a family of basket-weavers who live there still; they write often and play no part here. Prism's gift showed early but stayed small. A few years of lessons at the Grove School taught Prism what that gift could do and, mostly, what it could not: no great workings, no healing, nothing that would ever matter to a scholar. What it could do was make light. Small lights, soft and coloured, that move where Prism moves them and last a few breaths before they fade.

The forest has many people who can do more, and Prism never minded. What Prism minded was the forest's way of thinking that magic must be useful or sacred. Prism wanted to make pictures with it, for no reason except that they were lovely, and had heard of a city where nobody needs a reason. Two springs ago Prism walked out of the forest with a caravan of glass-carters and came to Urbanograd, and has been painting the air at the gate ever since.

### The Gate Walk

Prism chose the gate on purpose. The roads are frightening now, and travelers arrive tired, dusty and often shaken. Prism wants the first thing they see in Urbanograd to be something beautiful made just for them. The Gate Watch were doubtful at first, because lights in the dusk can be mistaken for other things, and Prism agreed to paint only inside the walls and never toward the road. Now the guards stop to watch, and Tick, Knox's son, who runs the gate's messages, salutes the herons.

The pictures are of the city's own stories: the Walkers' cart, the line of people with bundles, the first lanterns going up between the towers. Prism learned them by asking everyone in Urbanograd to tell them, which took a year and is not finished.

### Lux

Lux, the Keeper of the Lanterns, is Prism's friend. Prism is fascinated by the lanterns, by the colours of their glass and the way they make the old towers float in the dark, and asks Lux more questions about them in one evening than Lux usually answers in a year. Lux pretends to be worn out and, Prism suspects, secretly enjoys it. Some nights Prism climbs part of the round with Lux and paints small moths of light that follow the lantern-pole from tower to tower.

### Walkout Day

Prism's great hope is a light show for Walkout Day: after the play, when the square is full, a great picture painted across the whole dark sky above Lantern Square, the story of the Long Walk told in light. Lux has promised to help, dimming the lanterns at the right moment so that Prism's lights can be seen. The trouble is size. Prism has never made more than a handful of lights at once, and the show needs hundreds. Prism has been practising every night and has managed forty, briefly, before having to sit down.

Prism fears standing in front of the whole city on Walkout Day and making only a few small sparks. Prism also, quietly, worries about the forest; the news that comes from home is mostly cheerful, and not entirely.

A quest might find a way to make Prism's lights reach across the whole square, fetch something from the forest that could help, or keep the Walkout Day crowd from mistaking the show for something in the sky that should frighten them.
